t: Actions and approvals
x: MPAS represents a requested action as an Action Package: the execution payload, an envelope that binds it by a cryptographic digest, and approvals. t: Effects and privacy
x: A receipt proves what the signer of that receipt attested. It does not independently prove every action taken by a remote counterparty. Stronger end-to-end evidence may require the executing system to sign its own statement and still depends on the trust assigned to that system. An arbitrary external service cannot generally join an atomic transaction with the caller's local database. If an action was transmitted and the reply is lost, resending may duplicate it. The supported design is at-most-once dispatch with an honest indeterminate outcome when the external result cannot be resolved. It is not a universal exactly-once guarantee. The Action Package can expose the identities and decisions of its signers. Portable evidence is not automatically private evidence. The research identified threshold signing as a possible future direction, while leaving its compatibility with eligible-signer policy and evidence requirements unresolved. Research prototypes also showed that individually permitted results can leak information through their combination or through success-versus-failure outcomes. These are bounded observations about the named exercises, not measurements of every MPAS deployment.
